commits.subject: core, net: make duplicate constructor signatures reachable from C++Builder
commits.body:
Delphi emits W1029 when a class has two constructors with identical
parameter lists, since C++ constructors are anonymous and C++Builder
cannot tell them apart. The {$warn DUPLICATE_CTOR_DTOR OFF} in
mormot.defines.inc does not silence it when the units are compiled
into a package: it is reported against the .dpk (QC 100815), so every
package containing these units shows it.

- TFileStreamEx.CreateWrite() now takes an optional aShareMode
  parameter (default fmShareRead, the previous hardcoded value), which
  makes it distinct from CreateRead() and lets callers choose sharing
- THttpMultiPartDecoder.CreateFromContentType() takes an unused
  trailing aDummy parameter, as the VCL does with TCustomForm.CreateNew()

Existing calls compile and behave unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body: ex: duckdbproxy - DuckDB from 32-bit clients via a local Quack server
commits.author: ab

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+# duckdbproxy - DuckDB from 32-bit clients via a local Quack server
+
+DuckDB is only available as a 64-bit library. Since DuckDB 2.0, the `quack`
+extension can serve a database over HTTP with the
+[Quack protocol](https://duckdb.org/2026/05/12/quack-remote-protocol), and
+`mormot.db.sql.duckdb` includes `TSqlDBQuackConnectionProperties`, a pure
+Pascal Quack client which also works on Win32 and Delphi 7.
+
+So no Pascal proxy is needed: `duckdbproxy.dpr` launches the official 64-bit
+`duckdb` CLI with `TExternalProcess`, sends it `CALL quack_serve(...)` via
+stdin, then uses the database through the regular `TSqlDBConnectionProperties`
+API.
+
+```
+duckdbproxy [options]
+  --cli duckdb.exe      the 64-bit duckdb CLI executable
+  -d, --db <file>       the DuckDB database file - default is in-memory
+  -p, --port 9494       the local TCP port of the Quack server
+```
+
+## How it works
+
+```pascal
+server := TDuckDBQuackProcess.Create('duckdb.exe', 'data.duckdb', 9494);
+try
+  props := server.NewClient; // TSqlDBQuackConnectionProperties
+  try
+    // ... props.Execute() / props.ExecuteNoResult() as usual
+  finally
+    props.Free; // release the client (and its interfaces) first
+  end;
+finally
+  server.Free; // stdin EOF: the CLI checkpoints the database and exits
+end;
+```
+
+- The server only listens on `127.0.0.1`, with a random 128-bit token sent via
+  stdin, so it does not appear on the process command line.
+- `TExternalProcess` is started with `roCloseChildren`: the CLI is killed if
+  the client process ends without stopping it.
+- Other Quack clients, e.g. another DuckDB with `ATTACH 'quack:127.0.0.1:9494'`
+  or any language, can connect to the same server with the token.
+- The `quack` extension is downloaded by DuckDB on first use, unless it was
+  installed before (`INSTALL quack`).
+
+Tested with DuckDB 2.0.0 from Delphi 7, Delphi 13.1 (Win32 and Win64) and
+FPC 3.2.3 (Win64) clients.

@@ -0,0 +1,354 @@
+# dbbench - DuckDB vs SQLite3 vs PostgreSQL for analytics
+
+`dbbench` runs the same analytical queries on DuckDB, SQLite3 and PostgreSQL,
+all through the `mormot.db.sql` classes, so the numbers are what a mORMot
+application gets.
+
+It answers two questions:
+- when does DuckDB pay off compared with the usual mORMot storage engines?
+- how much SQL does each engine need for typical analytics?
+
+## The datasets
+
+Two datasets (`--dataset` option): a standard benchmark, and real open data.
+
+### `tpch`: the TPC-H benchmark
+
+[TPC-H](https://www.tpc.org/tpch/) is the reference benchmark for analytical
+(decision support) databases: 8 tables of a wholesale supplier (orders,
+line items, customers, parts, suppliers, nations, regions) and 22 queries.
+
+- **Reproducible:** the data is generated by DuckDB itself (`CALL dbgen(sf = 1)`),
+  without any download, and is the same on every computer.
+- **Scalable:** scale factor 1 is 6 million `lineitem` rows (about 1 GB of CSV),
+  10 is 60 million rows, and so on.
+- **Comparable:** DuckDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and many papers publish TPC-H
+  numbers. For a broader comparison of engines including SQLite and PostgreSQL,
+  see also [ClickBench](https://benchmark.clickhouse.com/) (100 million rows of
+  web analytics).
+
+### `rail`: the Dutch railways open data
+
+[Rijden de Treinen](https://www.rijdendetreinen.nl/en/open-data) publishes every
+train service of the Netherlands since 2019, with each stop, its delay,
+cancellation and platform change (CC BY 4.0): about 22 million stops and
+2.4 million services per year, as gzipped CSV.
+
+- **Real data with real questions:** punctuality, delays per station and hour,
+  cancellations - the kind of report an application has to produce.
+- **Normalized like an application database:** `sql/rail/load.duckdb.sql` splits
+  the CSV into `stations`, `services` and `stops` tables, as an ORM would store
+  them, so the queries join.
+- **Scalable:** `--years 2023,2024` loads several years (one file per year).
+
+### Loading
+
+`dbbench --prepare` loads the data with DuckDB (`dbgen` for `tpch`, `read_csv`
+over HTTPS for `rail`), then copies it into SQLite3 and PostgreSQL via DuckDB
+`ATTACH (TYPE sqlite)` and `ATTACH (TYPE postgres)`, so all engines hold exactly
+the same rows.
+
+## The queries
+
+All queries fetch all their rows. The numbers of each result are summed and
+compared between the engines: a `*` in the results marks a different result.
+
+### `tpch` queries
+
+| file | what | why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `q01` | TPC-H Q1, 8 aggregates over 98% of `lineitem` | full scan |
+| `q03`, `q10` | TPC-H joins of 3-4 tables with top N | join and sort |
+| `q05` | TPC-H 6-table join over one year | join order |
+| `q06` | TPC-H selective range, covered by an index | index-friendly |
+| `q12`, `q14` | TPC-H joins with conditional aggregates | |
+| `q18` | TPC-H group by over all `lineitem` in a sub-query | big hash aggregate |
+| `a1` | monthly revenue and 3-month moving average | window over an aggregate |
+| `a2` | top 3 customers per nation | top N per group |
+| `a3` | median and 90th percentile per priority | percentiles |
+| `a4` | revenue per year and ship mode | pivot table |
+| `a5` | revenue per region and nation with subtotals | rollup |
+| `a6` | most expensive order per priority | arg max |
+| `a7` | distinct customers per year and segment | count distinct |
+| `p1` | 10,000 point lookups by primary key | OLTP |
+| `p2` | 10,000 single-row inserts in one transaction | OLTP |
+
+### `rail` queries
+
+| file | what | why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `r1` | punctuality (arrivals less than 3 minutes late) per month and company | join of all stops |
+| `r2` | stations with the highest average departure delay | aggregate, then join |
+| `r3` | delay and late departures per hour of the day and train type | join, time functions |
+| `r4` | median and 95th percentile of the delay per train type | percentiles |
+| `r5` | cancell
... [truncated, 15238 more chars]

+-- (at least 10,000 departures), with the station name
+-- portable SQL: the same text for all engines - aggregating before the join
+-- allows SQLite3 to use the covering stops_station index
+SELECT code, name, departures, avg_delay
+FROM (
+  SELECT station_code, count(*) AS departures,
+    avg(departure_delay) AS avg_delay
+  FROM stops
+  WHERE departure_delay IS NOT NULL

+  HAVING count(*) >= 10000) delays

+ORDER BY avg_delay DESC

commits.subject: ex: duckdbproxy - DuckDB from 32-bit clients via a local Quack server
commits.body:
- launches the official 64-bit duckdb CLI with TExternalProcess, sends it
  CALL quack_serve() via stdin with a random token, then uses the database
  with the pure Pascal TSqlDBQuackConnectionProperties client
- no 64-bit Pascal proxy, no mormot.db.proxy: works from Win32 and Delphi 7,
  and other Quack clients in any language can connect to the same server
- roCloseChildren kills the CLI if the client process ends unexpectedly,
  and closing stdin lets the CLI checkpoint the database file and exit
- replaces the former mormot.db.proxy based duckdbproxy proposal, following
  https://github.com/synopse/mORMot2/issues/423#issuecomment-6791660513

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: db: DuckDB file import/export/convert methods
commits.body:
TSqlDBDuckDBConnectionProperties.FileToDocVariant, ImportFile, ExportSql
and ConvertFile let DuckDB read and write data files directly, with no
Pascal copy of the rows, the format being recognized from the file
extension: .csv .tsv .json .jsonl .ndjson .parquet .xlsx
- file names are bound as ? parameters (UTF-8, also on Delphi 7)
- read_xlsx() autoloads the excel extension: only COPY TO .xlsx needs an
  explicit LOAD excel, so no per-instance extension state is kept
- new TTestDuckDB.Files test: table -> CSV -> table with DATE/BOOLEAN
  sniffing, CSV -> TSV -> Parquet -> JSON -> TDocVariant, reader options,
  unknown extension, XLSX only if the excel extension is installed
- new "dbbench --files" mode comparing ExportSql/ImportFile/ConvertFile
  with a mormot.db.sql rows loop (FetchAllToCsvValues/FetchAllToJson)
- see https://github.com/synopse/mORMot2/issues/423

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: tf

     (the same SQL on all engines) - SQLite3 from 10.7 s to 1.7 s.
   - DuckDB needed no tuning.
 
+## Data files: DuckDB file methods vs a rows loop
+
+`TSqlDBDuckDBConnectionProperties` can let DuckDB read and write data files
+itself, the format being recognized from the file extension (`.csv` `.tsv`
+`.json` `.jsonl` `.ndjson` `.parquet` `.xlsx`):
+
+```pascal
+props := TSqlDBDuckDBConnectionProperties.Create('', '', '', ''); // in-memory
+props.ImportFile('customers', 'customers.csv');  // CREATE TABLE AS read_csv(?)
+props.ExportSql('from customers where sales > 1000', 'top.xlsx');
+props.ConvertFile('export.csv', 'export.parquet'); // COPY (read_csv(?)) TO ?
+rows := props.FileToDocVariant('data.xlsx', 'sheet = ''Data''');
+```
+
+`dbbench --files` compares them with the regular `mormot.db.sql` way, i.e.
+fetching the rows and writing them in Pascal (`FetchAllToCsvValues`,
+`FetchAllToJson`), on the first `--filerows` rows (1 million by default) of
+`lineitem` (16 columns), or `stops` for `rail`.
+
+Delphi 13.1 Win64, DuckDB 2.0.0, AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 6850U, TPC-H scale factor 1,
+1 million rows, best of 3 runs:
+
+| operation | DuckDB file method | mormot.db.sql rows loop |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| table -> CSV | **374 ms** (`ExportSql`) | 1.12 s (`FetchAllToCsvValues`) |
+| table -> JSON | 1.06 s (`ExportSql`) | **856 ms** (`FetchAllToJson`) |
+| CSV -> table | 469 ms (`ImportFile`) | - |
+| CSV -> Parquet | 503 ms (`ConvertFile`) | - |
+| Parquet -> table | 88 ms (`ImportFile`) | - |
+
+- DuckDB writes CSV 3 times faster, using several threads, but the JSON
+  output of mORMot is faster than the DuckDB one.
+- Importing a file creates a typed table (DuckDB detects e.g. DATE and BOOLEAN
+  columns in a CSV) with no row going through Pascal: there is no equivalent in
+  `mormot.db.sql`.
+- Parquet is the format to use between DuckDB instances: columnar, compressed
+  and typed, it is imported 5 times faster than CSV.
+- `.xlsx` needs the DuckDB `excel` extension: reading autoloads it, but it
+  should have been installed for writing (e.g. `INSTALL excel` once).
+
 ## SQL for analytics: DuckDB vs PostgreSQL vs SQLite3
 
 The `a*` and `r*` queries do the same thing on each engine; compare the files

commits.subject: ex: new dbbench comparing DuckDB with SQLite3 and PostgreSQL on analytics
commits.body:
- runs the same TPC-H and Dutch railways open data queries on DuckDB,
  SQLite3 and PostgreSQL, all through the mormot.db.sql classes, and also
  DuckDB over the SQLite3/PostgreSQL files (ATTACH) and a Quack server
- "dbbench --prepare" loads the data with DuckDB, then copies it into the
  other engines, so that all of them hold exactly the same rows
- results are checked between engines and written as a markdown table
- README documents the datasets, the queries and some reference results
- see https://github.com/synopse/mORMot2/issues/423

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,313 @@
+# dbbench - DuckDB vs SQLite3 vs PostgreSQL for analytics
+
+`dbbench` runs the same analytical queries on DuckDB, SQLite3 and PostgreSQL,
+all through the `mormot.db.sql` classes, so the numbers are what a mORMot
+application gets.
+
+It answers two questions:
+- when does DuckDB pay off compared with the usual mORMot storage engines?
+- how much SQL does each engine need for typical analytics?
+
+## The datasets
+
+Two datasets (`--dataset` option): a standard benchmark, and real open data.
+
+### `tpch`: the TPC-H benchmark
+
+[TPC-H](https://www.tpc.org/tpch/) is the reference benchmark for analytical
+(decision support) databases: 8 tables of a wholesale supplier (orders,
+line items, customers, parts, suppliers, nations, regions) and 22 queries.
+
+- **Reproducible:** the data is generated by DuckDB itself (`CALL dbgen(sf = 1)`),
+  without any download, and is the same on every computer.
+- **Scalable:** scale factor 1 is 6 million `lineitem` rows (about 1 GB of CSV),
+  10 is 60 million rows, and so on.
+- **Comparable:** DuckDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and many papers publish TPC-H
+  numbers. For a broader comparison of engines including SQLite and PostgreSQL,
+  see also [ClickBench](https://benchmark.clickhouse.com/) (100 million rows of
+  web analytics).
+
+### `rail`: the Dutch railways open data
+
+[Rijden de Treinen](https://www.rijdendetreinen.nl/en/open-data) publishes every
+train service of the Netherlands since 2019, with each stop, its delay,
+cancellation and platform change (CC BY 4.0): about 22 million stops and
+2.4 million services per year, as gzipped CSV.
+
+- **Real data with real questions:** punctuality, delays per station and hour,
+  cancellations - the kind of report an application has to produce.
+- **Normalized like an application database:** `sql/rail/load.duckdb.sql` splits
+  the CSV into `stations`, `services` and `stops` tables, as an ORM would store
+  them, so the queries join.
+- **Scalable:** `--years 2023,2024` loads several years (one file per year).
+
+### Loading
+
+`dbbench --prepare` loads the data with DuckDB (`dbgen` for `tpch`, `read_csv`
+over HTTPS for `rail`), then copies it into SQLite3 and PostgreSQL via DuckDB
+`ATTACH (TYPE sqlite)` and `ATTACH (TYPE postgres)`, so all engines hold exactly
+the same rows.
+
+## The queries
+
+All queries fetch all their rows. The numbers of each result are summed and
+compared between the engines: a `*` in the results marks a different result.
+
+### `tpch` queries
+
+| file | what | why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `q01` | TPC-H Q1, 8 aggregates over 98% of `lineitem` | full scan |
+| `q03`, `q10` | TPC-H joins of 3-4 tables with top N | join and sort |
+| `q05` | TPC-H 6-table join over one year | join order |
+| `q06` | TPC-H selective range, covered by an index | index-friendly |
+| `q12`, `q14` | TPC-H joins with conditional aggregates | |
+| `q18` | TPC-H group by over all `lineitem` in a sub-query | big hash aggregate |
+| `a1` | monthly revenue and 3-month moving average | window over an aggregate |
+| `a2` | top 3 customers per nation | top N per group |
+| `a3` | median and 90th percentile per priority | percentiles |
+| `a4` | revenue per year and ship mode | pivot table |
+| `a5` | revenue per region and nation with subtotals | rollup |
+| `a6` | most expensive order per priority | arg max |
+| `a7` | distinct customers per year and segment | count distinct |
+| `p1` | 10,000 point lookups by primary key | OLTP |
+| `p2` | 10,000 single-row inserts in one transaction | OLTP |
+
+### `rail` queries
+
+| file | what | why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `r1` | punctuality (arrivals less than 3 minutes late) per month and company | join of all stops |
+| `r2` | stations with the highest average departure delay | aggregate, then join |
+| `r3` | delay and late departures per hour of the day and train type | join, time functions |
+| `r4` | median and 95th percentile of the delay per train type | percentiles |
+| `r5` | cancell
... [truncated, 13161 more chars]

+-- the 10 stations with the highest average departure delay
+-- (at least 10,000 departures), with the station name
+-- portable SQL: the same text for all engines - aggregating before the join
+-- allows SQLite3 to use the covering stops_station index
+SELECT code, name, departures, avg_delay
+FROM (
+  SELECT station_code, count(*) AS departures,
+    avg(departure_delay) AS avg_delay
+  FROM stops
+  WHERE departure_delay IS NOT NULL
+  GROUP BY station_code
+  HAVING count(*) >= 10000) delays
+JOIN stations ON code = station_code
+ORDER BY avg_delay DESC
+LIMIT 10

commits.subject: net: FastCGI client refactoring from the #785 review
commits.body:
- the request is built into a TSynTempAdder instead of a
  TRawByteStringBuffer, with no heap allocation for most GET
- the URI path is decoded by DoUrlDecode() within a TSynTempBuffer, and
  validated by the loop which locates the script: no temporary string
- SCRIPT_NAME, SCRIPT_FILENAME and CONTENT_LENGTH are appended with no
  temporary string
- the HTTP_* variables are computed by a simpler FastCgiAppendHeaders()
- TFastCgiResponse.Output is a RawByteString appended by each record, as
  THttpRequestContext does for chunks: FastCgiParseOutput() removes the
  CGI headers from it, and it is sent as HTTP body with no copy
- TFastCgiHeader.RecType is a TFastCgiRecordType
- documented why HttpResponse needs a compare-and-swap
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: net: THttpProxyServer can relay requests to a FastCGI application - see #388
commits.body:
A Source like fcgi://127.0.0.1:9000/var/www sends each request to a
FastCGI responder application, e.g. php-fpm, and answers the HTTP client
via AsyncResponse() once the application response is complete.

- new TFastCgiAsyncConnection and TFastCgiAsyncConnections classes in
  mormot.net.proxy, over a TAsyncClient, with one connection per request
- AsyncResponse() has a new optional CustomHeaders parameter
- new THttpProxyServerSettings.AddFastCgi() method
